title: The Master Bards (Ki Men Guru)
cultural_context: Honorific phawar paying homage to the master village philosophers and archers, published in 'Ka Phawar Beh Sbai' (1997).
lyrics_khasi:
Ieng rwai, ieng phawar,
Ko ki Men Guru ba shida,
Ha ling-shad, ha lyngkha,
Ki thoh ki tar ba phyrnai;
La don ka stad ka jynrap
Ha kyntien ba ki kren,
Ban pynkhlain ia ka jaidbynriew
Ha ka hok bad ka jingshisha.

Ki la iehnoh ka spah
Ba palat ban ia ka ksiar,
Kato ka akor babha
Ba ri u Hynniew Trep;
To kynmaw ia ki,
Haba ngi rwai phawar,
Ban pynim ia ka ktien
Ha ki paitbah baroh.
lyrics_english:
Arise and chant, arise and rhyme,
O master bards of humble heart,
In dancing arenas and farming fields,
Their verses sparkle bright;
Wisdom and understanding dwell
In every word they utter,
Strengthening the nation
In righteousness and truth.

They bequeathed a treasure
Priceless beyond gold,
That pristine moral conduct
Cherished by the Seven Huts;
Let us remember them
Whenever we chant our phawars,
To keep alive our language
Among all the populace.
